Quantum entanglement is a physical phenomenon that occurs when a group of particles is generated, interact, or share spatial proximity in a way such that the quantum state of each particle of the group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, including when the particles are separated by a large distance. It is significant in physics because it challenges classical notions of locality and realism, demonstrating that measurements performed on one part of an entangled system can instantaneously affect the state of another part, regardless of the distance between them. This property is fundamental to emerging technologies such as quantum computing, quantum cryptography, and quantum teleportation.
